instruction.text: Are these statements true or false?

atoms.a: Elderly people have better vision than young people.

feedback.finish: Vision typically gets worse as you get older. It becomes harder to focus on objects that are close to you, and more light is needed to be able to read.

atoms.a: Elderly people have worse hearing than young people.

feedback.finish: Hearing also gets worse as you get older — especially for high-pitched sounds.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The body is made up of cells that also age over time. Eventually, they die and get replaced by new cells. When we get older, this process of cells being replaced slows down.

Organs, such as the heart, are made up of cells. When the system of cell replacement slows down, the organs work less effectively. This means that elderly people are more likely to get ill because their organs do not work as well.
Elderly people’s bones also become more fragile. The organs in their digestive system stop working as well, so they cannot absorb the calcium that is needed to have strong bones.
